edits.target: asks for the title or category noun itself (Dalai Lama), not the individual named in the clue.
edits.content:
- 'X & this <actor/person>' ('Lemmon & this actor joined an all-girl band', 'Laurel & this comedian'): X is an anchor already given. The answer is the OTHER member of the pair or group. Take the co-star or partner the passages list with X in the same sentence or cast line ('Tony Curtis and Jack Lemmon'). Do not repeat X, and do not answer with the film, the character or the group name.
- 'His/her name was X, but others called him this' / 'known to most as this': the answer is the OTHER name, title or role the passages give the character ('Zeb' -> 'Grandpa'). Never repeat the name already in the clue, and do not stretch the answer with a surname or extra words ('Grandpa Walton').

edits.target: - Otherwise, build the answer from passages that match several of the clue's details.
edits.content: - Definition, term or etymology clues ('referred to by this term', 'this unit is equal to...', 'This adjective ... comes from the Latin for "before behind"'): look for the dictionary, glossary or etymology line that paraphrases the clue or quotes its literal gloss ('Apogee: the farthest point from the Earth in the Moon's orbit'; 'Man-hours: an industrial unit equal to the work one person can do in an hour'; 'literally "before-behind"'). The headword being defined, often in a page title or shared by several entries, is the answer. Copy it in singular dictionary form ('Man-hour', 'Apogee', 'preposterous') and keep the part of speech the clue names. Do not answer with the Latin or Greek root or a synonym.

edits.target: Still apply the person-name rule above.
edits.content: - Person-name form: (a) if a verbatim archive line gives a bare surname or short form ('... of "The Maids" | Genet.'), the answer is exactly that ('Genet'), not an expanded 'Jean Genet'. Copy the archived form, even when it is shorter than a full name. (b) Without a verbatim hit, give the plain 'First Last' form a trivia key would list, as the passages repeat it ('Joel Chandler Harris', 'Jessica Savitch', 'Marilyn Monroe'). Never use the encyclopedia headline form with extra middle names, suffixes or a nickname in quotes ('Marion Barry', not 'Marion Shepilov Barry, Jr.'; 'Tony Williams', not 'Anthony Allen "Tony" Williams'). Do not add titles, roles or descriptors, and do not shrink the name to a first name or bare surname unless an archive line shows that form.
